T4.2.message: In this line yoga is a spiritual practice paired with tapas as a way to reach Śiva. The chosen dictionary sense, 'the act of yoking, joining', is the first and literal sense in mw-yoga.md (p. 856,2), about harnessing horses, and it is wrong here. mw-yoga.md (p. 856,3) has the sense that fits: 'application or concentration of the thoughts, abstract contemplation, meditation ... the means by which the human spirit may attain complete union with Īśvara'. It also has the Pāśupata (Śaiva) sense 'the union of the individual soul with the universal soul'. Both translations agree with this reading: shlokam-vedasara-shiva-stava.md has 'attained by Tapas (penance) and Yoga', and gitapress-stotraratnavali.md has 'तप तथा योगसे प्राप्तव्य'. The word's displayed meaning, 'yoga', is fine; only the recorded sense is wrong.
T4.2.suggested_fix: Set sense.gloss to the MW p. 856,3 sense: 'application or concentration of the thoughts, abstract contemplation, meditation' (optionally adding the Pāśupata sense 'union of the individual soul with the universal soul'). Keep 'the act of yoking' only as the etymology, which the root gloss 'to join, to yoke' already gives.
